title: Seasonal steric variance ratios had no clear difference in three NOAA basin means for 2005-2025
abstract: We tested whether the total-to-thermal steric variance ratio differs by calendar season in NOAA upper-700-m basin means for 2005-2025. After removal of fixed season means and a linear trend, Atlantic ratios ranged from 0.598 to 0.822. All four marginal 95% intervals included one. A centered whole-year block bootstrap test gave a tail fraction of 0.579 for seasonal differences. Two- and four-year blocks gave 0.624 and 0.631. Pacific and Indian tests also gave no clear difference. Ratio levels depended on detrending. This null result does not prove equal seasonal responses. Only 21 years, one mapped product, source error, and bootstrap assumptions limit inference. Original code, aggregate basin evidence, all draws, source hashes, a figure, and audits support reproduction.

display.caption: Seasonal total-to-thermal residual variance ratios and marginal 95% three-year block limits. All limits include one. These are basin means, not local variances.
